name: Moose
caption: Won the XHCW World Television Championship from Chris Jacobson, 13 January 2002, then lost it to Steve Liermann at Counterstrike; later won the World Tag Team Championship with Anthony Dolarhyde at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Shawn Borders
caption: Lost a Table Ironman Match to Moose, four falls to three, at Retribution, 7 January 2002, and later dropped a Barbed Wire Ladder Match to a debuting Nailz and a Leather Strap Match to Nailz at Counterstrike.

name: John Sebastion
caption: Won the XHCW World Tag Team Championship with Scotty Fitzpatrick in a Double Dog Collar Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, lost it at Counterstrike, and made his last appearance in this pack at Unleashed, 16 March 2002.

name: Scotty Fitzpatrick
caption: Won the XHCW World Tag Team Championship with John Sebastion at Retribution, 7 January 2002, lost it at Counterstrike, and was eliminated first from the four-way dance for the vacant title at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Jolted
caption: Lost the XHCW World Tag Team Championship with Frost in a Double Dog Collar Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, and lost a "Losers Leave XHCW" tag match on 30 March 2002 without ever being shown leaving.

name: Frost
caption: Lost the XHCW World Tag Team Championship with Jolted in a Double Dog Collar Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, and lost a "Losers Leave XHCW" tag match on 30 March 2002 without ever being shown leaving.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with records held in other promotions; no roster or document ties this billing to any of them.

name: 2Short
caption: Lost the XHCW World Light Heavyweight Championship to Kletus Casady in a Cage Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, then won the World Tag Team Championship with Adam Simon at Counterstrike, billed as "Short and Long."

name: Kletus Casady
caption: Won the XHCW World Light Heavyweight Championship from 2Short in a Cage Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, then lost it to Chris Cage twelve days later.

name: Steve Liermann

tenures.note: Billed on the promotion's own 15 April 2002 notice as one of three top XHCW players signed on a trial contract; the 19 April card calls him a famous multi-time champion in other promotions.

caption: XHCW's own president and a wrestler: helped The Juice retain the World Heavyweight Championship at Retribution, 7 January 2002, revealing the stable Absolute Power; won the World Television Championship from Moose at Counterstrike, and lost it to Duff Man at Affliction.

identity.note: The same name recurs in a Top 200 poll record, a 2003 cross-federation tournament card and a 2002 Superslam guest record, each already held apart from the others; no document ties any of the four together.

name: Marcus Wilson
caption: Lost a Clean Match to "Sadistic" Steve Liermann at Retribution, 7 January 2002.

identity.note: The same name, and this promotion's own record already cites Windy City RAW's Resurrection pay-per-view as XHCW's own 2001 relaunch point; no moniker or roster note on the WC-RAW record to corroborate further. Probable, not proven. (earlier assertion: possibly)

name: Chris Jacobson
caption: Won the XHCW World Television Championship from Chris Cage at Retribution, 7 January 2002, and lost it to Moose six days later.

name: Chris Cage
caption: Lost the XHCW World Television Championship to Chris Jacobson at Retribution, 7 January 2002; won and lost the World Light Heavyweight Championship twice more across the year, ending it as champion no longer after Hardcore Harvest.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with records held in other promotions; no roster or document ties this billing to any of them.

name: Adam Simon

tenures.source: The promotion's own Grand Debut Exhibition of 7 May 2002, its Talkin' Smack packet of 13 May 2002, its title-tournament first round of 18 May 2002 and its Call to Arms of 23 August 2002.

tenures.note: Billed on the promotion's own 15 April 2002 notice as one of three top XHCW players signed on a trial contract; he defends the Undisputed Universal title on 3 May.

caption: Won the XHCW TransAtlantic Championship from Pico Flush in a Texas Death Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, later won the World Tag Team and World Heavyweight Championships, and lost the Heavyweight title to Brad Jones at Affliction.

name: Pico Flush
caption: Lost the XHCW TransAtlantic Championship to Adam Simon in a Texas Death Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002.

name: The Dehibilitator
caption: Retained the XHCW World Hardcore Championship over "Ironman" James Loyal in a Last Man Standing Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, held it through the winter, lost it to Nailz at Unleashed, and fell through a broken railing in a no-result Scaffold Match at Affliction.

identity.note: The other record is a WWA/FWA wrestler from 2000, an unrelated house style two years earlier; no document ties the two together.

name: James Loyal
caption: Lost a Last Man Standing Match for the XHCW World Hardcore Championship to The Dehibilitator at Retribution, 7 January 2002, when his own knee gave out on the ten count.

name: The Juice
caption: Won the XHCW World Heavyweight Championship from "Sadistic" Steve Liermann at Awakening, 26 November 2001, retained it over Duff Man at Retribution with Absolute Power's help, lost it to Adam Simon at Unleashed, and turned on Liermann himself at Affliction.

name: Duff Man
caption: Lost the XHCW World Heavyweight Championship match to The Juice at Retribution, 7 January 2002; later won the World Television Championship from Steve Liermann at Affliction, and the World Heavyweight Championship from Vincent Lyons at Hardcore Harvest.

identity.note: The other record is a 2008 fed six years later; no document ties the two together.

name: Brad Jones
caption: Debuted at Retribution, 7 January 2002, revealing the stable Absolute Power; won the TransAtlantic Championship at the Silverdome, and the World Heavyweight Championship from Adam Simon at Affliction.

name: J-Dub
caption: Lost a Weapons Match to Brad Jones at Assault, 13 January 2002, and a debut match to The Scorpio at Counterstrike.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a record on another promotion; no document ties the two together.

name: Trevor Finnell
caption: Debuted by interrupting a match at Assault, 13 January 2002; won the 15-Minute Table Ironman Match a week later, joined the on-screen stable DeX at Counterstrike, and turned heel on 2Short, 7 April 2002.

name: Too Damn Tough
caption: Debuted in an impromptu brawl at Assault, 13 January 2002, and beat "Heinous" Lee Friedman in a Glass Table Match at Counterstrike.

name: Kid Furious
caption: Debuted on the microphone at Assault, 13 January 2002, and lost the 15-Minute Table Ironman Match to Trevor Finnell a week later.

name: "Heinous" Lee Friedman
caption: Debuted running in to help Duff Man against The Juice, 13 January 2002, and lost a Glass Table Match to Too Damn Tough at Counterstrike.

name: Homicide
caption: A masked attacker who debuted jumping Trevor Finnell backstage, 2 February 2002, and lost a hardcore brawl to him at Counterstrike, still unidentified.

identity.note: A common hardcore-wrestler ring name held by several unrelated promotions and one aka collision; no document ties this masked debut to any of them, and no real identity is ever given in this pack.

name: Nailz
caption: Debuted with a Barbed Wire Ladder Match win over Shawn Borders, 2 February 2002; won the World Hardcore Championship from The Dehibilitator at Unleashed and held it past Hardcore Harvest.

name: Vincent Lyons
caption: Debuted with a mafioso gimmick, 2 February 2002; won the vacant TransAtlantic Championship at Affliction, and the World Heavyweight Championship off-page, losing it as "Aftermath" to Duff Man at Hardcore Harvest.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a record on a community hub; no document ties the two together.

name: Midnight Rider
caption: Debuted as a wrestler in a Non-Title Bullrope Match against The Dehibilitator, 19 January 2002, having previously appeared only as a masked attacker.

name: The Scorpio
caption: Debuted with a win over J-Dub at Counterstrike, 9 February 2002; turned heel and joined Absolute Power on 30 March 2002 after a Steel Cage main event loss to Ramsus Palantiri.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with several held records, including an unassigned bare-name stub with no corroborating detail; no document ties this billing to any of them.

name: Ramsus Palantiri
caption: Debuted attacking Adam Simon post-match, 2 February 2002; won the World Light Heavyweight Championship off-page and returned radically changed at Hardcore Harvest, dropping the TransAtlantic Championship to the mat unclaimed.

name: Fudgey McGlone
caption: Debuted on the 5 March 2002 lineup; won the World Television Championship from Kryptonic at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a 2003 record on another promotion; no document ties the two together.

name: Super Skit
caption: First scheduled for a match on the 5 March 2002 lineup; lost the World Light Heavyweight Championship match to Ramsus Palantiri at Unleashed.

name: Godfather
caption: Debuted on the 5 March 2002 lineup and lost to Vincent Lyons on 30 March 2002 after Steve Liermann's interference backfired.

identity.note: Shares its billed name (and, on one held record, an aka) with several unrelated promotions' mafioso-gimmick wrestlers; no document ties this billing to any of them.

name: Robert Wallace
caption: Debuted on the 5 March 2002 lineup, losing to Frost.

name: Jin Rico
caption: Debuted with a win over Robert Wallace, 30 March 2002.

name: Chia
caption: Lost the XHCW World Hardcore Championship match to Nailz, 30 March 2002.

name: Jeremy Cross

tenures.note: Billed on the promotion's own 15 April 2002 notice as one of three top XHCW players signed on a trial contract; debuts on 19 April.

caption: Introduced via flashback at Unleashed as the one who threw Chris Jacobson off the stage at Counterstrike; won his first proper match, a squash over The Great White Pope, 30 March 2002.

name: The Great White Pope
caption: A one-off jobber, lost a squash match to Jeremy Cross, 30 March 2002.

name: Static Death
caption: Debuted with a win over Trevor Finnell, 7 April 2002, and reached the TransAtlantic Championship tournament semifinal at Affliction before losing to Fear.

name: Krimzon Fury
caption: Debuted interfering for Chris Cage, 7 April 2002, becoming his new tag partner, informally "Sudden Impact."

name: Skullberry
caption: Debuted in a 3-way Light Heavyweight Championship match at Counterstrike, eliminated first.

name: Wes Copeland
caption: A free agent signed by president Steve Liermann, introduced in a vignette as "The Apostle" at Assault, 7 April 2002; never booked a match in this pack.

identity.note: The aka "The Apostle" collides with a held record's own name; no document ties this free-agent signing to that record.

name: Will Jaxson
caption: A free agent introduced cutting a promo at Assault, 7 April 2002, bragging of his own standing over a fellow new signing; never booked a match in this pack.

name: The Butcher
caption: Lost a hardcore brawl to Midnight Rider at Unleashed, his only appearance in this pack.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a record on another promotion; no document ties the two together.

name: Khan
caption: Debuted turning on Moose to help Steve Liermann win the World Television Championship at Counterstrike, 9 February 2002, revealed as Absolute Power's newest member.

identity.note: The same name; this promotion's own record already cites Windy City RAW's Resurrection pay-per-view as XHCW's own November 2001 relaunch point, and this debut follows a few months later. No moniker or roster note corroborates further. (earlier assertion: possibly)
Shares its billed name with further unrelated records; no document ties this debut to any of them.

name: Simon Kempthorne
caption: Debuted losing to Matt Barry at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: Matt Barry
caption: Debuted with a win over Simon Kempthorne at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: Tronix Tidan
caption: Debuted losing to Jay Aguilera at Hardcore Harvest, then was attacked by a debuting Jeffery Fisher.

name: Jay Aguilera
caption: Debuted with a win over Tronix Tidan at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, and was recruited into DeX by Jeffery Fisher.

name: Jeffery Fisher
caption: Debuted attacking Tronix Tidan and recruiting Jay Aguilera into DeX at Hardcore Harvest, then beat a debuting Maxx Payne.

name: Maxx Payne
caption: Debuted losing to Jeffery Fisher at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, then attacked both Fisher and Aguilera.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a record on another promotion; no document ties the two together.

name: The Terminator
caption: Appeared in a Home Invasion video segment, 16 October 2002, under the gimmick name T-1000, before being eliminated with Trevor Finnell from the four-way dance for the vacant World Tag Team Championship at Hardcore Harvest.

identity.note: A common gimmick name held by numerous unrelated promotions; no document ties this billing to any of them.

name: Slade
caption: Eliminated with Raine Temple, last out of the four-way dance for the vacant World Tag Team Championship at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Raine Temple
caption: Eliminated with Slade, last out of the four-way dance for the vacant World Tag Team Championship at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Anthony Dolarhyde
caption: Won the vacant World Tag Team Championship with Moose in a four-way dance at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, with manager Paul Wade's interference.

name: JohnMan
caption: Eliminated with Scotty Fitzpatrick, first out of the four-way dance for the vacant World Tag Team Championship at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Paul Wade
caption: Manager to Moose and Anthony Dolarhyde, revealed at Hardcore Harvest as having smuggled them into the four-way dance they won for the vacant World Tag Team Championship.

name: Spiral
caption: Debuted as a mystery opponent already holding Chris Cage's own World Light Heavyweight Championship, winning it at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: Apathy
caption: Chris Cage's newer valet, whose botched interference cost him the World Light Heavyweight Championship at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: Micheal Graves
caption: Lost an Xtreme Tables, Ladders and Chairs Match for the World Hardcore Championship to Reverend Death at Hardcore Harvest.

name: Reverend Death
caption: Retained the World Hardcore Championship over Micheal Graves in an Xtreme Tables, Ladders and Chairs Match at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: Liselle Maragravine
caption: Ramsus Palantiri's new valet, introduced at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, when he returned radically changed.

name: Fear
caption: Debuted in the TransAtlantic Championship tournament at Affliction, 28 April 2002, reaching the final before losing to Vincent Lyons.

identity.note: A common gimmick name held by several unrelated promotions; no document ties this debut to any of them.

name: JT Damon
caption: Interfered against The Dehibilitator in the no-result Scaffold Match at Affliction, 28 April 2002.

name: Invection
caption: The Dehibilitator's valet, billed alongside him through his matches from January to April 2002.

name: Faith
caption: Chris Cage's valet, billed alongside him through his matches from January to April 2002.

identity.note: A common valet/wrestler name held by several unrelated promotions; no document ties this billing to any of them.

name: Stacy Keibler
caption: Steve Liermann's valet, billed alongside him through his matches from January to April 2002.

name: Willow
caption: Duff Man's valet, billed alongside him at Unleashed and Hardcore Harvest.

identity.note: Shares its billed name with a record on another promotion; no document ties the two together.

name: Kryptonic
caption: Appeared in a Home Invasion video segment, 16 October 2002; won the World Television Championship from Duff Man off-page, and lost it to Fudgey McGlone at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

identity.note: An eleven-month gap from Windy City RAW's own close, longer than this promotion's other Windy City RAW guards; no document ties the two together.

name: Baby Scarface
caption: Introduced himself in a roleplay promo, 31 January 2002, as a free agent signed by president Steve Liermann after Alpha Championship Wrestling's own closure; no booked match found in this pack.

identity.note: Shares the distinctive word "Scarface" with several unrelated promotions' bare-named records; no document ties this signing to any of them.
